To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

farmers’ perceived importance of personal protection and farmers’ safe behavior in pesticide spraying were influenced by the same variables: knowledge of pesticide toxicity (positive effect on personal safety importance and safe behavior), education (positive effect on perceived importance of personal security), age (positive effect on both variables), and farm size (positive effect on safe behavior).
farmers with high education and small farm size, who perceived high risk and high usefulness of PPA, showed high perception of personal safety and high safe behavior in PPE usage.

(1) farmers who are more educated and have more land are less likely to perceive low importance of personal protection in pesticide spraying, (2) farmers who have more knowledge about pesticide risks, are more educated, and have more land, and are less likely to show unsafe behavior in P.P.E. use in pesticide spraying, and (3) the most common predictors of both variables are the perception of risks, knowledge about pesticide risks and farm size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the factors that affect the perceived importance of personal protection and safe behaviors of farmers in terms PPE use during spraying pesticides.

the drivers of personal safety in agriculture, which is an important step towards understanding the factors influencing farmers’ safety behavior and developing interventions that will increase the use of personal protective equipment in pesticide spraying.
understanding the drivers of personal safety in agriculture and can help in the design of interventions aiming at promoting personal safety among farmers and farm workers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

farmers who have a high knowledge of pesticide toxicity and a high risk perception are the ones who will be more likely to have high perceived importance of personal protection and safe behavior in terms PPE use.
personal safety in agriculture is a complex phenomenon and requires a multifaceted approach to be addressed.
the most important factor for improving personal safety in agriculture is to increase the knowledge of pesticide toxicity and risk of pesticides among farmers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

farmers should be educated to be more self-confident, to be more aware of pesticide risks, and to follow their colleagues’ behaviors in order to increase the perceived importance of personal protection and the safe behavior in pesticide use.
the most important drivers of personal safety in agriculture are the perception of risk, the knowledge of pesticide toxicity and the farm size.
the more farmers perceive the risk of pesticide use, the more they are likely to perceive the importance of personal safety as well as to follow safety measures in their daily work.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of PPE in pesticide application can be improved by increasing the perceived risk of pesticides and by improving farmers’ knowledge of pesticide toxicity and usefulness of PPE in reducing pesticide exposure.
education and training programs should be developed to promote knowledge about pesticide risks and to improve personal safety in agriculture.
farmers should always be encouraged to take personal safety measures during pesticide spraying, even in cases where they do not feel that there is a risk.
